properties.name: Cabrillo passes this coast northbound
properties.summary: The first European ships along this shore, standing well out; no landing on this stretch. Ferrelo repassed in 1543. Course generalized (interpretive).

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Cabrillo relation (Wagner, Spanish Voyages to the Northwest Coast).

properties.name: The Manila ships' landfall run
properties.summary: Returning galleons made their American landfall to the north and ran south along this coast for Acapulco, year after year for two and a half centuries. Course generalized (interpretive).

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Schurz, The Manila Galleon.

properties.name: Drake careens in a 'faire and good Baye'
properties.summary: Five weeks ashore among the Coast Miwok. The landing site is a famous fight; Drakes Bay is the prevailing identification and the one the exhibit panel follows.
properties.notes: Site identification debated; shown at Drakes Bay per the panel.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; The World Encompassed (1628); cf. the site controversy literature.

properties.name: The San Agustin wrecks under Cermeno
properties.summary: The Manila ship sent to survey the coast anchored in the bay behind Point Reyes and was driven ashore; the crew ran south in an open launch, surveying as they went. Her porcelain cargo still washes into Coast Miwok sites.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Wagner, 'The Voyage of Cermeno' (CHS Quarterly, 1924).

properties.name: The San Carlos inside the Golden Gate
properties.summary: Ayala brings the first ship through the Gate by night and anchors off the island he names for Our Lady of the Angels; forty-four days inside the bay while Canizares surveys it by longboat.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Galvin ed., The First Spanish Entry into San Francisco Bay, 1775.

properties.name: The bay discovered from Sweeney Ridge
properties.summary: Ortega's scouts, hunting Monterey, stumble instead onto 'a great arm of the sea': the first European sight of San Francisco Bay. The whole strategic geography of Alta California changes in an afternoon.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Crespi diary, ed. Brown, A Description of Distant Roads.

properties.name: The turning-point camp on San Francisquito Creek
properties.summary: The expedition's council under the tall redwood (the palo alto): short of food, they turn back south for San Diego.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Crespi diary, ed. Brown.

properties.name: Monterey occupied; the coast re-walked
properties.summary: With Monterey finally recognized and occupied, the 1769 trail up the coast is re-run to probe the new bay.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Crespi diary, ed. Brown.

properties.name: First Europeans at the Carquinez strait
properties.summary: Marching up the eastern bayshore, Fages and Crespi reach the narrows where the whole interior drains to the sea, and look across at the mouths of the great rivers.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Crespi diary, ed. Brown.

properties.name: Palou's cross at Point Lobos
properties.summary: Rivera and Palou walk the peninsula to its tip and plant a cross above the Gate: the marker Ayala's men will find standing the next summer.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Palou diary (Bolton, Historical Memoirs of New California).

properties.name: Anza's first overland party reaches Monterey
properties.summary: The Sonora road proved: Alta California can be reached, and colonized, overland.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Bolton, Anza's California Expeditions.

properties.name: The presidio site chosen at the Gate
properties.summary: Font: a table-land commanding the narrows, 'the harbor of harbors.' The white cliff above the Gate becomes the presidio of San Francisco that autumn.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Font's complete diary (Bolton, Anza's California Expeditions IV).

properties.name: The arroyo de los Dolores chosen for the mission
properties.summary: The sheltered creek and lagoon two leagues in from the Gate, named for the Friday of Sorrows: the site of Mission San Francisco de Asis, where these exhibit panels hang today.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Font's complete diary (Bolton IV).

properties.name: To the mouths of the rivers
properties.summary: Anza and Font round the southern bay, run the eastern shore past the strait, and look into the delta before turning for home: the whole future mission-and-presidio geography seen in one circuit.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Font's complete diary (Bolton IV).
